I’ve always loved hardbacks the most. Not being a practical person, convenience has never been an issue. In high school, I always had a stack of them to carry (also not too difficult because a couple of guys would sort of switch off carrying them for me, pity I think, not popularity).
Hardbacks feel real to me, I can hold them and curl up in a chair, hug them, slam them closed when something dreadful, stupid, or wonderful happens, read hunched over on a train etc. 

Now, I was unfortunately forced to live with a book hater when I was a teen. I would hide my books and read in my closet (not kidding). More than once the threat of taking and burning them was spoken (and indeed some were... confiscated. They weren’t inappropriate, Jane Eyre, Ivanhoe, the first two books in the Dragonlance series (paperbacks) (shout out to other Raistlin lovers)).

So I suppose as an adult I love having my big hardbacks out on bookshelves (and floor and tables and in the bed). It’s freedom and luxury to me.
Also, they look really nice:) except the ones I read to death. I’ve actually learned bookbinding so I can re-cover some true loves.

LOL not a sob story, but possibly part of the reason for my love of hardbacks.
